statusText: Mapped policy state: EA_ON. Tail is 6 of 100 in the low band, nineteen points below the 25-point block threshold, because the CME weekend closure is now exactly twenty-four hours old and removes the very price path this score measures. Stress holds at 53 in the elevated band: Riyadh withholding retaliation at Iraq's request and a three-day repair precedent for an earlier pipeline attack offset the Houthi consolidation at Bab el-Mandeb and firmer odds of a Wednesday rate increase. Confidence holds at 87, because the index level, VIX, the H.15 curve, crude, the FOMC calendar and the Hormuz diplomatic track were each re-verified against primary sources this hour.
recommendation: Tail sits deep in the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and a green status, and the single shared reading applies to both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Three observations support it. First, Friday's completed path granted mean reversion rather than denying it: the Nasdaq-100 closed 29,368.44, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, about 105 points below its 29,473.12 high inside a 159.61-point cash range, and VIX fell 11.21% to 15.84. Second, CME equity index futures have been halted since 21:00 UTC Friday and do not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, two hours after the final slot of this horizon closes, so no slot in the forward window can contain the persistent no-retracement structure that Tail measures. Third, the unresolved items are supply-side and policy-side rather than structural: the shut East-West pipeline, the Houthi position at Bab el-Mandeb, Monday's Salalah meeting and a live FOMC week are all carried in Stress, which alone does not change the mapped state. No danger window is published, because narrow evidence-based windows are preferred and no hour inside a closed market qualifies.
headline: Twenty-four hours into the CME weekend halt the Nasdaq-100 still stands at its 29,368.44 Friday close with VIX 15.84 and WTI marked $100.05, while Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline stays shut after drones launched from Iraq's Maysan province, Iranian state media report explosions off Qeshm Island, and Monday's Salalah meeting is not expected to produce a signed Hormuz agreement ahead of a Wednesday FOMC decision priced near a 90% chance of a 25 basis point increase.
body:
The price picture is unchanged, as expected across a closed weekend, and was re-verified against primary sources this hour. The Nasdaq-100 quote page shows a 29,368.44 close, up 264.93 points or 0.91%, inside a 29,313.51 to 29,473.12 range against a 29,103.51 previous close, so the cash range spanned only 159.61 points and the close finished about 105 points below the high, roughly 4.5% under the 30,762.20 fifty-two-week high. VIX is 15.84, down 11.21% from 17.84, having settled near the 15.59 low of a 15.59 to 17.71 range. The latest H.15 observation, for 10 September, shows the 2-year at 4.56%, the 5-year at 4.75%, the 10-year at 4.95% and the 30-year at 5.37%, with the federal funds effective rate at 3.63%. WTI is marked $100.05, down 2.37% on the day but up 9.7% on the week and 20.15% on the month, with Brent $104.61, down 2.81%.

Three items were verified this hour and they broadly offset. Reporting on the East-West pipeline confirms it was moving four to five million barrels a day, was shut precautionarily after Friday's drone strikes on equipment near Riyadh and Medina, and has no published restart date; the same reporting notes that an earlier 2026 attack on a pumping station was repaired within three days and that Riyadh is withholding retaliation at Iraq's request, both of which argue against an open-ended outage. Against that, Iranian state media reported two explosions off Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz on Saturday afternoon, and Houthi forces completed their capture of Yemen's Red Sea coast on Friday, consolidating control of Bab el-Mandeb, the alternative route for Saudi barrels. On the policy side, the week-ahead reporting puts implied odds of a 25 basis point increase at Wednesday's FOMC near 90% after Friday's inflation print, a touch firmer than the reading carried an hour ago. Net of these, Stress is unchanged at 53.

One structural item was added to the week-ahead picture rather than to the current scores. Index reporting indicates SpaceX's Nasdaq-100 weighting rises at the quarterly rebalance as lock-up expiries expand its free float, with an estimated $15.5 billion of associated passive buying. The rebalance adjustments fall at Friday's U.S. close, well outside this 24-hour horizon, so the item is carried as a week-ahead flow consideration in Stress and in the event calendar, not as current Tail evidence.

The forward horizon runs from 21:00 UTC Saturday to 20:00 UTC Sunday and lies entirely inside the closure; the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC Sunday, two hours after the final slot closes. Conditional Tail therefore opens at 6 and steps to a ceiling of 16 in the final slot, tracking accumulating unpriced weekend headline exposure rather than any observed structure. Every slot stays inside the low band, so EA_ON and green apply throughout and no danger window is published. Shared Finviz context collected at 21:05 UTC is delayed, latest-session evidence only: it shows Friday's NQ 0.86% higher, VIX futures 8.41% lower, seven of eight megacaps higher and semiconductors mixed-to-firm. That backdrop is aligned but calm, and under the evidence rules it supports Confidence rather than raising Tail.

lookbackSummary: All twenty-four clock-hours from 21:00 UTC on 11 September to 20:00 UTC on 12 September carry a published Claude assessment, so every lookback slot is available and none is reconstructed. The window opens at the moment of the CME futures halt with Tail at 7 and Stress in the high band at 68, still decaying from Friday's CPI print. Tail fell to 5 by 00:00 UTC and has since held a 5 to 6 band in normal mode across every remaining slot, tracking the closure rather than any directional view. Stress decayed steadily from 68 to a 50 trough at 17:00 UTC, then firmed to 52 and 53 as the Qeshm Island explosions and the Iranian signal on Monday's Salalah meeting were verified. Confidence held a narrow 85 to 89 band throughout, reflecting a complete but static evidence set.
outlookSummary: Every one of the twenty-four forward slots lies inside the CME weekend closure that began at 21:00 UTC on Friday, and the reference contract does not reopen until 22:00 UTC on Sunday, two hours after this horizon's final slot closes. Conditional Tail opens at 6 in the current slot, the only slot containing observed rather than hypothetical structure, then steps gradually to a ceiling of 16 as unpriced weekend headline exposure accumulates ahead of the reopen. Every slot stays inside the low band, so the deterministic mapping returns EA_ON and green throughout, and no danger window is published. Stress traces a shallow U, easing to 52 across the dead overnight hours and firming to 58 in the final slot as Monday's Salalah meeting and Wednesday's FOMC decision approach without any weekend venue in which to price them. Confidence dips to 84 mid-horizon, where the last observed price path is furthest behind and no new data exists, then recovers to 87 as pre-reopen indications and completed weekend reporting arrive.
